localHook: Pomona is one of the Inland Empire’s most historically layered cities—and that layering shows up directly in the restoration work. The historic downtown core and the Ganesha Hills neighborhoods hold homes from the 1920s and 1930s: original plaster construction, galvanized supply lines, cast-iron drain stacks, and plumbing configurations that predate modern building codes by several decades. When a joint fails inside a plaster wall in a 1928 Pomona bungalow, the moisture behavior is fundamentally different from a drywall failure—it travels through the lathe structure, absorbs into original wood framing, and sets up mold conditions inside assemblies that are difficult to access without damaging finish materials. Ganesha Hills and Pomona’s northeastern foothills carry wildfire exposure that has intensified as regional fire activity has increased. Hillside runoff during heavy rain periods pushes water toward lower-elevation residential lots along Phillips Ranch and downtown. Gallagher Restoration has been on SR-60 to Pomona for over 15 years.

neighborhoods.heading: Historic downtown to the foothills—Pomona covered

items.name: Historic downtown Pomona
items.body: Dense residential and mixed-use blocks with 1920s–40s construction. Galvanized plumbing, plaster walls, and cast-iron stacks are the norm here. Water-damage assessment in these properties requires specific protocols for older construction materials to avoid unnecessary damage to original finishes.

items.name: Phillips Ranch
items.body: Planned residential community with 1970s’80s tract construction and slab foundations. Copper supply lines are in or approaching the failure window. Storm drainage can be a secondary concern when hillside runoff from adjacent terrain exceeds neighborhood drainage capacity.

items.name: Ganesha Hills
items.body: Hillside community with direct wildfire exposure and a mix of mid-century and newer construction. Fire and smoke are the primary damage vectors. HVAC decontamination following smoke events is a recurring need in this elevated terrain.

items.title: Aging historic plumbing in downtown homes
items.body: Pomona’s 1920s and 1930s housing stock carries original or early-replaced plumbing that is now 80 to 100 years old. Galvanized supply lines corrode from the inside out; cast-iron stacks develop pinhole failures. Moisture inside plaster walls moves through lathe structure and into framing in ways that require careful, complete assessment before any drying protocol begins.

items.title: Hillside wildfire exposure and smoke infiltration
items.body: Ganesha Hills and the northeastern foothills face increasing wildfire risk as regional fire seasons intensify. Smoke and soot infiltration embed in HVAC systems and porous materials during nearby fire events. Full post-fire decontamination—not surface cleaning alone—is required to address embedded soot and odor.

items.title: Hillside runoff and ground-level water intrusion
items.body: Hard rain events push runoff from Pomona’s hillside terrain toward lower-elevation residential lots. Garages, lower floors, and crawl spaces absorb ground-level intrusion faster than drainage infrastructure can discharge it. Gallagher responds during active storm events to begin extraction before secondary damage compounds.

items.title: Slab leaks in Phillips Ranch tract homes
items.body: 1970s and 1980s copper supply lines embedded in concrete slabs throughout Phillips Ranch are approaching or inside the failure window. Silent slab leaks raise water bills and migrate moisture under flooring for weeks before visible signs appear. Professional moisture detection locates the source efficiently.

pricing.heading: Honest numbers on restoration cost in Pomona
pricing.body: Assessment is free. Most residential restoration jobs in Pomona fall between $1,500 and $18,000 depending on damage category, affected materials, and discovery timing. Historic construction in the downtown core can trend toward the upper range when plaster walls and original framing require careful, low-impact drying protocols to preserve finish materials. Slab-leak responses depend on whether subfloor replacement is required. Wildfire smoke jobs vary based on HVAC involvement and soot infiltration extent. Gallagher works directly with major insurance carriers and prepares all adjuster documentation.
